Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid Delta renewal & capacity uplift — proposed pricing pathway

Maya — thanks again for today's QBR. A few follow-ups after reviewing your Q1 usage (attached) and the expansion ask you shared: an incremental 30% baseline capacity increase across embeddings and chat, and a desire to lock pricing while you complete a procurement approval.

High-level proposal for discussion:
- Term: 18 months (start date aligned to existing renewal window)
- Committed capacity: 30% uplift applied as a blended commit across workloads
- Discounting: 18% off list for committed units; additional 3% rebate if usage exceeds committed baseline for two consecutive quarters
- Credits: one-time $40k onboarding/ingestion credit to offset data migration costs
- Price hold: 6-month price hold on per-token rates, then a quarterly true-up tied to a cap of +6% on list price
- Flex: optional burst pool (shared metered pool) at a fixed uplift rate to avoid unpredictable overages

Attached: orchid_delta_usage_report_Q1.csv (usage breakout) and a first-draft amendment (proposed_amendment_v3.pdf). 

Two asks from us: 1) confirm procurement timeline so we can align DocuSign cadence, and 2) confirm whether the finance team needs a show-back cost model (we can produce a short one-pager).

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the thoughtful proposal and the usage file. A few initial points from our side: 

- Term: We prefer a 24-month lock if possible — longer term helps our board visibility around unit economics.
- Discounting: 18% is a good start but we need a path to 22% at scale (either staged milestone or volume tier).
- Price hold: Can you extend to a 12-month firm price hold? Our procurement folks are uncomfortable with a 6-month window.
- Credits: The $40k ingestion credit is appreciated; can some of that convert to a quarterly applied credit to reduce cashflow impact in Q3?

I looped in procurement to vocalize timing — we can get legal review started next week if we have the commercial language finalized. Also please include an explicit breakdown of committed vs. burst pricing for embeddings — that was a recurring question in today's session.

Maya

Looping Marcus (finance) on Orchid Delta's counter. Short notes:
- 24-month term request — finance preference is 18 months given pricing uncertainty, but Marcus can run guardrails for 24 months if we layer in a limited floor/ceiling or a mid-term cadence for model/quant adjustments.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orchid Delta renewal & capacity uplift — proposed pricing pathway

Thanks Priyom — quick finance take: 

1) 24 months: acceptable only if we include a mid-term true-up at 12 months tied to usage mix and a firm cap on per-token increases (+6%). That protects us from model-cost swings.
2) Discount ramp: agree to the staged approach (18% baseline; +2% at QPS threshold; +2% at annual committed volume) but require clear, measurable thresholds in the amendment to avoid ambiguity.
3) Credits: convert $40k ingestion credit into a $20k upfront + $20k applied as quarterly invoice credits over the first 4 quarters — helps both cashflow and accounting.
4) Burst pool: define burst as metered at a 1.6x uplift on committed per-token rate; include usage guardrail to prevent unlimited exposure (notify at 80% of burst spend).

If Priyom and Naomi agree, finance can draft redline language for the amendment and I can sign off on the commercial. Also recommend we attach a one-page cost model for them (simple monthly projection) before procurement kicks off.

-Marcus
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference

Maya — thanks for the prompt feedback and for looping procurement. Per our internal review, here's a commercial summary we can take to legal: 

- Term: 24 months, with a contractual mid-term review at month 12 (usage true-up).
- Committed uplift: +30% baseline across chat + embeddings (blended commit).
- Discounting: 18% off list at contract signature; +2% at 3M QPS threshold; +2% at first anniversary if annual committed volume is met — net up to 22%.
- Price hold: 12-month firm price hold, then quarterly adjustments not to exceed +6% per year on list price (contract includes cloud-cost-link clause).
- Credits: $20k upfront credit + $20k applied as equal quarterly invoice credits over first 4 quarters.
- Burst pool: available at 1.6x uplift over committed unit rates; automated spend alarms at 80% consumption.

Next steps: 1) If this aligns, we'll prepare a redlined amendment and a short cost model for procurement. 2) I'll open the HubSpot deal stage to "Draft Amendment" (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/9843) and initiate DocuSign once legal confirms language.

If procurement wants earlier cashflow relief, we can discuss a modest prepayment schedule tied to the upfront credit.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this finalized.

Best,
